summary: Recorded receipt 78769a572c5b4b249e441ac7ce63422a, the transfer-state probe built to settle where the earlier in-progress error came from. In both cases the demoted follower's own configuration reported the non-voter role before the call, the leader's transfer flag read false before the call and at every later sample, the request completed with no error, and the named member never reported Leader across more than 280 samples; the single case had no leaderless sample, the retry case had about 60 ms of them, and leadership ended on a different member both times. The account keeps conclusion violated and defect claimed, and the rationale now states that the library accepted a demoted member as an explicit target and reported the transfer as complete while never installing it, so the surface the caller sees is success rather than a refusal. The limitation that could not attribute the in-progress error is replaced with the narrower finding that the flag was clear when each request was issued, so no pre-existing transfer explains it, and this harness does not reproduce the error at all because its retry case stopped after the first successful attempt. A new counterevidence entry records that the earlier error is therefore an unexplained surface rather than a stable consequence of naming a non-voter, leaving the durable claim that neither outcome is a suffrage-keyed refusal and neither installs the target. Both transfer knowledge entries gain the receipt, knowledge-0 on the case events and knowledge-1 on the result events, at the resulting revision.
